identity.name: Strata Finance
identity.does: Packages distress-refinance files for UK SMEs with stacked short-term debt and HMRC arrears.

houseRules: Strata packages; it does not lend.
No rates, APR, guarantees, instant approval, or we-lend claims.
Do not tell a visitor they are eligible.
Time to Pay is an instalment arrangement, not a loan.
Teach structures, do not name lenders as villains.
Sales TTP page and Learn TTP article are different URLs.

path.title: What a commercial payday lender actually is
path.excerpt: An informal name for very short-term, high-cost business credit — and why it stacks.

path.title: Poor cashflow will kill the business on its own
path.excerpt: The current account is the oxygen. Sort that before anyone sells you another facility.

path.title: Time to Pay is not time to hide
path.excerpt: An instalment arrangement with HMRC, not a loan, and not a place to disappear.

path.title: How to avoid a warehouse broker
path.excerpt: If they will not name the lender, they are selling inventory.

handbook.title: If the business is in trouble, start here
handbook.excerpt: A director's map for the first 48 hours — what to stop doing, what to read, and which help is real.

quizzes.question: A broker says they can get money in by Monday if you pay a commitment fee today. What should you do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pay the fee so the offer does not expire.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop signing, write down who you already owe, and ask the four questions in writing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sign the personal guarantee "just to get the offer out".

choices.label: D
choices.text: Let them send the pack to every lender they know, then decide.

quizzes.explain: Same-day pressure is a sales tool. A file that cannot be written down is not ready to be leveraged again.

quizzes.question: HMRC is chasing, and a VAT return is still unfiled. Can you hide behind a Time to Pay request?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes — asking for Time to Pay pauses everything.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. The return comes first. Time to Pay is not a place to hide.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, if a broker files it for you.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only if you also take a short-term facility to show "intent".

quizzes.explain: HMRC Time to Pay is an instalment arrangement after the liability is visible. Unfiled returns are the opposite of that.

quizzes.question: Who is real help on a Thursday afternoon, and who is a product?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A warehouse broker who wants a card payment today.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Business Debtline, or a licensed insolvency practitioner's first conversation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any firm that rang you offering to "save the company".

choices.label: D
choices.text: A lead-gen turnaround site that will not name the person you will speak to.

quizzes.explain: Free charity advice and a licensed IP are help. A same-day broker is selling inventory.

quizzes.question: You want to pay the supplier you like, and leave HMRC and a quiet lender waiting, because the supplier shouted. What is the risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: None — directors can choose who to pay.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A preference claim, if the company is insolvent or bordering on it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only a problem if you pay yourself.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only a problem after a winding-up order.

quizzes.explain: Moving money to a favoured creditor when the company cannot pay everyone is how preference claims get built. Read the danger-zone lesson before you move cash.

quizzes.question: What four things should you get in writing from a broker before they go to market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their logo, a testimonial, a LinkedIn, and a mobile number.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lender name, product, every fee, and the commission in pounds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A same-day decision and a "soft search" pack.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A personal guarantee template "for later".

quizzes.explain: If they will not name the lender and the commission, they are selling a product they already have, not packaging a file.

quizzes.question: What is Strata, in one sentence you should be able to repeat?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A lender that specialises in distress.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A packager of files. It does not lend.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A turnaround firm that takes appointments as administrator.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A broker that holds a warehouse of same-day products.

quizzes.explain: House identity is not decoration. If a page here ever sounds like a lender, it has gone wrong.

handbook.title: Warehouse brokers
handbook.excerpt: How a call-centre broker actually gets paid, why they will not name the lender, and the questions that end the pitch.

quizzes.question: A broker will not name the lender, but wants a commitment fee today. What is happening?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are matching you carefully to a panel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They already have a product. You are the inventory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Same-day funding is how high-street banks work now.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Naming the lender would breach confidentiality until you sign.

quizzes.explain: A packager can name the proposed lender. A warehouse is selling stock. The fee is to stop you walking before the commission drops.

quizzes.question: Which three income lines can sit on the same warehouse file?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Your fee, the lender's commission to the broker, and the resale of your data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interest, VAT, and stamp duty.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the fee on the invoice they send you.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only what Companies House shows as a charge.

quizzes.explain: The fee you see is one line. Commission and lead-sale are the other two. Ask for the commission in pounds.

quizzes.question: Dual charging — a fee from you and a commission from the lender — is automatically unlawful in commercial finance. True or false?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True. Any second payment is a bribe.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False. It is common. The problem is concealment, a false claim of independence, and packing the fattest kickback.

choices.label: C
choices.text: True, but only if the loan is over a certain size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: False, and you should never ask about it because it is confidential.

quizzes.explain: Commercial dual charging is common. Concealment and a pretend independent role are the problem. Wood is the case. Get the number in writing.

quizzes.question: "We'll restructure the existing stack" from a warehouse usually means what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They will negotiate a single longer facility and cancel the sweeps.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They will add another short-term product whose collections sit on top of the ones you already cannot pay.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They will file a Time to Pay for you.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They will take an administration appointment.

quizzes.explain: Restructuring, in that mouth, is a new product. Read stacked debt before you sign it.

quizzes.question: What belongs in an email to a broker before anyone goes to market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A scanned driving licence and a card number.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lender legal name, product in one sentence, every fee in pounds, commission in pounds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Permission to submit to any lender they like.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A signed personal guarantee "to speed things up".

quizzes.explain: If they cannot answer those four in writing, they are not packaging a file.

quizzes.question: Your mobile starts ringing with firms you never contacted, twenty minutes after the first broker call. What happened?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The market is competitive and they all found you independently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Your data was sold down an introducer chain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Companies House publishes mobile numbers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a sign the deal is strong.

quizzes.explain: A packager does not need to sell your mobile to eat. A warehouse does.

quizzes.question: A broker agreement says they are not your agent and give no advice, but the call said they were on your side. What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Trust the call. The agreement is standard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Treat the document as the truth, and walk if it does not match the pitch.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sign, because oral promises override terms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tick the independent legal advice box without ringing a solicitor, to keep things moving.

quizzes.explain: The agreement is what gets read later. The call is what gets you to sign. Put the pen down.

handbook.title: Hidden commissions
handbook.excerpt: Secret fees, half-secret small print, Wood, Hopcraft, and why a 2025 Supreme Court case is not a magic claim for every commercial director.

quizzes.question: A broker's terms say they "may receive a fee from lenders" and will tell you the amount in writing before you complete. They never send the amount. After Wood, how should you treat that commission?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As half-secret, so there is nothing you can do.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As fully secret, because you were entitled to proceed as if no commission was being paid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As automatically a Consumer Credit Act claim.

choices.label: D
choices.text: As lawful, because "may receive" is enough disclosure.

quizzes.explain: Wood held that a promised written figure that never arrived left the borrowers off notice. The commissions were secret, not half-secret.

quizzes.question: What did the Supreme Court actually do in Hopcraft in August 2025?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It held that every undisclosed motor-finance commission is a bribe.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It held that typical motor dealers do not owe a fiduciary duty of loyalty, so the bribery and equity claims failed. One claimant still won under the Consumer Credit Act.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It extended Wood to every introducer in the United Kingdom.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It banned lender commissions.

quizzes.explain: Hopcraft pulled the law back. Dealers selling cars are not impartial brokers. Johnson won on unfair relationship, not on bribery.

quizzes.question: Why is Plevin a dangerous case to wave at a commercial facility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is not a real case.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a consumer PPI unfair-relationship decision. Most SME facilities are not in the Consumer Credit Act.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It only applies in Scotland.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It abolished secret commissions.

quizzes.explain: Plevin is about PPI and s.140A. It is not a template for unregulated commercial credit. Ask a solicitor whether your agreement is in scope before you build a plan on it.

quizzes.question: A warehouse broker told you they were independent and would find the best deal. The terms say they are not your agent. Which story is closer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hopcraft — they were obviously a salesman.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wood — they held themselves out as impartial, then took a lender payment you were not told about.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither. Oral pitches never matter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only FCA rules matter, and commercial brokers are never in court.

quizzes.explain: The pitch can create the duty Wood talked about — honest and impartial information or recommendation. The terms are an attempt to write it away. Get advice on the facts.

quizzes.question: What should you have in pounds, in writing, before you are bound?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only the monthly collection, because commission is confidential.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every fee you pay, and every commission the lender pays the broker.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nothing. Asking is rude.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only what appears on a Companies House charge.

quizzes.explain: Pounds, in writing, before you are bound. "We may receive a fee" is not a number.

quizzes.question: Is an undisclosed commission automatically a bribe after 2025?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, always.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. It depends on the duty the intermediary actually owed, and on whether any unfair-relationship statute applies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, but only for companies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, and therefore you should never ask.

quizzes.explain: Hopcraft restored orthodoxy. Secret payments to someone who owed you impartiality are one thing. Payments to a salesman who never pretended to be your agent are another. Ask, then get advice.

handbook.title: HMRC Time to Pay
handbook.excerpt: An instalment arrangement, not a loan, not a right, and not a place to hide. What HMRC actually looks at, and what happens if you break it.

quizzes.question: What is HMRC Time to Pay?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A loan from HMRC at a special rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An instalment arrangement for tax you already owe. Not credit, not a right.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automatic breathing space for any limited company that asks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A write-off if you keep paying something.

quizzes.explain: Time to Pay is collection by instalments. It is not credit and not a right. HMRC either believes you cannot pay on the due date, or they enforce.

quizzes.question: For business taxes, what does HMRC's own manual say about duration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Two to five years is standard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It should be less than 12 months. Longer is exceptional.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lasts as long as the new facility you are about to take.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is no guidance.

quizzes.explain: DMBM800040: business-tax Time to Pay should be under 12 months except in exceptional, manager-authorised cases. Do not model a refinance on a plan HMRC has not agreed.

quizzes.question: A VAT return is unfiled. Can you use Time to Pay as cover?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Asking pauses penalties.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. File first. Time to Pay is not a place to hide.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, if a broker calls HMRC for you.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only for Corporation Tax.

quizzes.explain: The liability has to be visible. Unfiled returns are the opposite of an instalment arrangement.

quizzes.question: Why did Crown preference coming back in 2020 change distressed refinance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It did not.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Certain VAT, PAYE and NICs are secondary preferential in insolvency, so treating HMRC as just another unsecured creditor is out of date.

choices.label: C
choices.text: HMRC can no longer petition to wind a company up.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time to Pay became a legal right.

quizzes.explain: Finance Act 2020 restored Crown preference from 1 December 2020 for specified taxes. A packager who still treats HMRC as ordinary unsecured is not reading the file.

quizzes.question: You take a short-term sweep "to catch up HMRC" and then miss the Time to Pay anyway. What have you done?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shown good faith. HMRC will wait.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Put a second collector on the same cash. The insolvency is later, and worse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Created a regulated consumer-credit agreement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nothing, as long as the broker filed the plan.

quizzes.explain: Stacking a sweep on top of a tax schedule is how broken Time to Pay arrangements are born. Offer HMRC a number you can keep without a fantasy facility.

quizzes.question: Is Time to Pay the same as breathing space or a company moratorium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes — all three freeze creditors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. Breathing space is for individuals. A Part A1 moratorium is a different company tool with a monitor. Time to Pay is HMRC only.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, if HMRC agrees.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Time to Pay is the company moratorium.

quizzes.explain: Three different tools. Mixing them up is how directors miss the one that might actually help.

handbook.title: Terms that should stop the pen
handbook.excerpt: All-monies, additional security on demand, a personal guarantee that never dies, and the boxes you ticked without a solicitor in the room.

quizzes.question: An all-monies clause means what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The security covers only this facility.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The security can cover everything you owe that lender, now or later, not just this facility.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The lender must release the charge when this facility is paid.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It only applies to property mortgages.

quizzes.explain: All-monies turns a single facility into a pipe. Ask what it takes to release the charge and the guarantee.

quizzes.question: The offer expires in twenty minutes and the independent-legal-advice box is blank. What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tick it. Everyone does.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Do not tick it. Let the offer expire if they will not wait for a solicitor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask the broker to initial it for you.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tick it, then ring a solicitor next week.

quizzes.explain: The certificate is a statement that you understood. Ticking it without advice is how that statement gets used against you.

quizzes.question: Cross-default on a stacked file does what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing, unless a court orders it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turns a missed payment to someone else into a default under this facility too.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protects you from other lenders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only applies to HMRC.

quizzes.explain: One local miss becomes a simultaneous acceleration. Distressed companies should not collect cross-defaults like stamps.

quizzes.question: A personal guarantee is "continuing", "on demand", and "joint and several". Can they come for you before they have finished with the company?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No. They must liquidate first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes. That is what those words are for.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only if you were the majority shareholder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only if the facility was a personal regulated credit agreement.

quizzes.explain: On demand and joint and several means they can pick the deepest pocket first. The company being "in process" is not a shield.

quizzes.question: The broker promised on the call that they would renew at the same price. The document has an entire-agreement clause. Where does the promise live?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the call. Courts always prefer oral evidence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nowhere, unless it is in the document.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the broker's CRM.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the Companies House charge.

quizzes.explain: Entire agreement and non-reliance are there to kill the call. If it matters, it goes in the document.

quizzes.question: Additional security on demand is "standard" according to the broker. What is it actually?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A courtesy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lever to demand the house, a spouse, or shares, and to treat a refusal as default.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Illegal in commercial contracts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only enforceable after a CCJ.

quizzes.explain: On a distressed day they use it. Cap it, or walk.

quizzes.question: The only way out of the facility is a "renewal" with a new fee on the remaining balance. What do you have?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A normal working-capital line.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A subscription to your own debt, not an exit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Time to Pay.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A regulated consumer-credit relationship by default.

quizzes.explain: A renewal fee on the residual is how you still owe more than you borrowed after months of collections. Put the pen down.

handbook.title: Products that finish companies
handbook.excerpt: Daily sweeps, stacked short-term credit, bridging used as working capital, and "renewals" that are just a new fee. Structures, not brand names.

quizzes.question: A daily sweep feels "flexible" on a busy Saturday. What does a quiet Tuesday tell you?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing. Daily is always cheaper.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The operating account is no longer yours in practice. The product has to work on the quiet week, not the best week.

choices.label: C
choices.text: HMRC will treat the sweep as a Time to Pay.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Quiet days are not collected.

quizzes.explain: Sweeps price risk by taking cash first. If the residual cannot pay VAT and wages, the product does not fit. A second sweep will not fix that.

quizzes.question: What is stacking?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Refinancing several facilities into one longer structure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two or more short-term collectors on the same cash, each taking a fee.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Filing two VAT returns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having a current account and a savings account.

quizzes.explain: Stacking is extra collectors, not a refinance. A warehouse "restructure" that adds a product is stacking with better branding.

quizzes.question: Bridging used to pay wages and VAT is usually what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A normal working-capital tool.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A property product with a defined exit, being used as same-day working capital — which is how it becomes an insolvency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A regulated consumer-credit agreement automatically.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Time to Pay.

quizzes.explain: Bridging needs a contracted take-out. "We'll extend" is not an exit.

quizzes.question: You have paid collections for months. They offer a "renewal" with a new fee on the remaining balance. What has happened?

choices.label: A
choices.text: You have reached a genuine working-capital relationship.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You are being sold a subscription to the same debt.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The old facility is legally gone even if the balance is not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fee is always refundable.

quizzes.explain: A renewal fee on the residual is how you still owe more than you borrowed. Pay down, refinance onto something that lasts, or take insolvency advice.

quizzes.question: Why does this lesson not name lenders?

choices.label: A
choices.text: There are no problem products.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The structure is what does the damage. Brand names are how you buy a libel letter instead of a better file.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FCA forbids naming companies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strata is a lender and cannot comment.

quizzes.explain: Structures, not logos. Once you can see the shape, you do not need the letterhead. Strata packages; it does not lend.

quizzes.question: Invoice finance plus the whole ledger plus an all-asset charge plus a continuing personal guarantee is a sign of what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A lender that loves the book.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lender that does not want to rely on the book alone — they want the company and the director too.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A standard current-account overdraft.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A product that never notifies debtors.

quizzes.explain: If they want the ledger and the house, believe the security pack, not the pitch.

handbook.title: Directors in the danger zone
handbook.excerpt: Sequana, wrongful trading, preferences, overdrawn loan accounts, and the minutes a court will actually want to see.

quizzes.question: After Sequana, when does the creditor duty switch on?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As soon as there is any real risk of insolvency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When directors know or ought to know the company is insolvent or bordering on insolvency, or that insolvent liquidation or administration is probable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only after a winding-up order.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never, because duties are always to shareholders.

quizzes.explain: The Supreme Court rejected a "real risk" trigger. Bordering on insolvency, or probable insolvent process. When the process is inevitable, creditors are paramount.

quizzes.question: What is the core of wrongful trading under section 214?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any loss-making year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuing once you knew or ought to have concluded there was no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvent liquidation, without taking every step to minimise loss to creditors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Filing a VAT return late.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taking a personal guarantee.

quizzes.explain: The switch is "no reasonable prospect". The duty is "every step". Minutes and licensed advice are how you show it.

quizzes.question: You pay the supplier you like, and leave HMRC and a quiet lender waiting, because the supplier shouted. What claim is that inviting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing. Directors choose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A preference, especially if the company is insolvent and the payment is influenced by a desire to prefer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only fraudulent trading.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only a consumer-credit claim.

quizzes.explain: Section 239. Connected parties are worse. Shouting is not a legal order of priority.

quizzes.question: An overdrawn director's loan account in a liquidation is what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drawings, so it vanishes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Money the company can call, treated as an asset the liquidator will chase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A dividend by another name, always lawful.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Protected if you called it wages on WhatsApp.

quizzes.explain: An overdrawn DLA is a debt you owe the company. Liquidators collect it.

quizzes.question: The COVID-era suspension of wrongful trading still protects you in 2026. True or false?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False. That relief expired. Do not rely on a 2020 memory.

choices.label: C
choices.text: True for Bounce Back Loans only.

choices.label: D
choices.text: True if HMRC agrees.

quizzes.explain: Temporary wrongful-trading relief was a pandemic measure. It is not a standing shield.

quizzes.question: What belongs in the minutes if you think the duty is on?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A slogan about being a fighter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cash, HMRC, the stack, licensed advice with a date, and a decision to continue for a defined reason or to open a process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the broker's name.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nothing. Minutes can be used against you, so write none.

quizzes.explain: If the only record is WhatsApp with a warehouse, that is the record. Write the adult version.

handbook.title: Help that is actually there
handbook.excerpt: Business Debtline, licensed insolvency practitioners, HMRC, the Ombudsman, the company moratorium — and the firms that ring you first.

quizzes.question: Business Debtline just rang your mobile offering to save the company for a fee. What is going on?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That is how they work now.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is not them. They never cold-call, never WhatsApp, and never charge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pay them. Charity numbers get reused.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ask them to take the administration appointment.

quizzes.explain: Money Advice Trust is explicit. They do not call first and they do not charge. Hang up.

quizzes.question: Who can take a company into administration, a CVA, or a Part A1 moratorium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any turnaround consultant with a good website.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A licensed insolvency practitioner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A warehouse broker with a panel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: HMRC automatically.

quizzes.explain: Formal insolvency tools run through licensed IPs. First conversations are often without a fee. Use GOV.UK to find one.

quizzes.question: A limited company can use the Debt Respite Scheme ("breathing space") to freeze creditors. True or false?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False. Breathing space is for individuals. Companies have a different tool: the Part A1 moratorium, with a monitor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: True if turnover is under £6.5 million.

choices.label: D
choices.text: True if HMRC agrees.

quizzes.explain: Mixing up individual breathing space with the company moratorium is how directors miss both.

quizzes.question: How long is the initial Part A1 moratorium?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 20 business days, extendable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Until HMRC is paid.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Until the warehouse facility lands.

quizzes.explain: Twenty business days, with a licensed monitor, to structure a rescue — not a product a broker can sell on a call.

quizzes.question: Can every SME take a commercial-finance complaint to the Ombudsman?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, always.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. Size tests apply, the firm must be in jurisdiction, and a lot of business-purpose credit sits outside the FCA perimeter.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, if you have a personal guarantee.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because the Ombudsman closed in 2019.

quizzes.explain: Micro-enterprise and small-business tests, plus FCA perimeter. "We'll go to the Ombudsman later" is not a plan for an unregulated sweep.

quizzes.question: What is the first free call if you are a director with personal exposure and a company in trouble?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The warehouse that rang you.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Business Debtline on 0800 197 6026, then a licensed IP if the company itself needs a process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A claims-management firm waving Plevin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A lead-gen "rescue" ad.

quizzes.explain: Charity first for the personal map. Licensed IP for the company. Packager after that, if there is still a file. Strata packages; it does not lend.

handbook.title: Stacked debt
handbook.excerpt: How the same cash gets pledged three times, why "one more facility" is the hole, and the sequence that actually stops the digging.

quizzes.question: A broker offers to "restructure" two existing sweeps by adding a third facility. What is that?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A refinance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stacking, unless the new money actually clears the old collectors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Time to Pay.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A company moratorium.

quizzes.explain: Restructure means the old collectors leave. A new collector on the same cash is a stack.

quizzes.question: Why draw a quiet-week cash page before you speak to anyone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To impress HMRC with a graphic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the residual is already negative after the existing collectors, a new collector cannot fix it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lenders require colour charts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You should not. It is demoralising.

quizzes.explain: The quiet week is the truth. Best-week stories are how stacks get sold.

quizzes.question: Three lenders each have all-monies and cross-default wording. What is the practical effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing until a court consolidates them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: One miss can accelerate more than one facility, and paying "this line" may not release the house.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The first lender to call wins everything automatically.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cross-default is unenforceable against companies.

quizzes.explain: Stack plus those clauses is a simultaneous problem. Map priority and releases in writing.

quizzes.question: What is the first move on a stacked file?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sign the renewal so you have time to think.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop signing, then write the map of collectors, HMRC, security and guarantees.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Let the warehouse submit you to the whole panel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pay the supplier who shouted, from the VAT.

quizzes.explain: The next signature is the hole. The map is the file. Packaging comes after.

quizzes.question: Using a new sweep to "catch up HMRC", then missing HMRC anyway, does what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Proves good faith.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Puts another collector on the tax money and makes the later insolvency worse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Creates an automatic Time to Pay.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moves HMRC down the priority list.

quizzes.explain: HMRC wants money arriving, not a new Direct Debit competing with them. File and schedule first.

quizzes.question: When is a new facility actually a replacement, not a stack?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the broker uses the word restructure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When it pays out the old collectors, kills their Debits, and releases security and guarantees you did not mean to keep — in writing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When it is same-day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the logo is different.

quizzes.explain: Replace means the old collectors leave. Everything else is branding.

tools.title: Debt Stress Check
tools.excerpt: Income, outgoings, facilities; cost per trading day; stacking flag.

tools.title: Time to Pay Calculator
tools.excerpt: Indicative monthly instalment. HMRC sets terms. 60-month cap under £250k arrears.

quiz.question: Still trading, cash is drowning, a broker can get a facility in 24 hours. What do you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take it. Oxygen first, structure later.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop. Map every facility, HMRC, and the personal guarantee before anyone new is paid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sign whatever they email today so Friday wages clear.

quiz.explain: Same-day money is how the stack starts. Strata packages files; it does not lend. Read the books before another name hits the current account.

quiz.question: The same broker rings. The first facility is already eating the account. They can get you more. What do you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Take the second facility so you can keep the first one current.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ask who the lender is and what it costs in pounds — then do not stack.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Roll the first one into a larger version of the same product.

quiz.explain: Loan two does not pay off loan one. It sits on top of it. Strata packages; it does not lend.

quiz.question: You are now borrowing to service the last loan. Friday wages almost do not happen. What is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A growth facility that needs time to bed in.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A refinance that will settle once turnover recovers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A trap. Stacked short-term credit servicing itself.

quiz.explain: Borrowing to service the last loan is the definition of a trap. Strata packages files. We do not lend.

beats.title: The house is on a personal guarantee

quiz.question: 3 a.m. The spreadsheet. The house is on a personal guarantee. What is the way out?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Another facility, larger, from a better-sounding broker.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A hard look at the books, then a packager who will not stack you further.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hide from HMRC until someone says yes.

quiz.explain: The way out is not another facility. Do not stack your way out of a hole. Strata packages; it does not lend.

beats.title: Don't stack your way out of a hole
